t: Variant: Final of the first act, instead of scene XVIII
Variant: Duet finale at the beginning of No. 18
d: Street with Bartolo's house on one side, with workable door and also workable window, closed by jealousy.
Figaro with a guitar behind his back, singing cheerfully, with a card and pencil in his hand, and said hidden.
Rosina from the window, then Bartolo, and hidden sayings.
The Count and Figaro return.
Bartolo from the house, and hidden sayings.
The Count and Figaro return.
Rosina's room, with various doors and window locked by a jealousy. Rosina writes at a coffee table, then Figaro.
Figaro and Rosina.
Bartolo in anger, and Rosina.
Bartolo alone.
The Awakeful comes yawning asleep, and said.
The young man arose as an old man, leaning on a reed and sneezing several times, and sayings.
Bartolo, Don Basilio coming, and Figaro listening in the background.
Figaro coming out of the toilet, then Rosina.
Bartolo returns, and said.
The Count in military uniform, pretending to be a little ubiquitous, and sayings.
Bartolo and Rosina.
Rosina alone, watching if he left.
Versione di Napoli, Teatro dei Fiorentini, 1787.
Camera as in Act I, scene VII.Bartolo, solo.
The Count in a bacchelier's dress, and that's it.
The Count alone.
Rosina with Bartolo, and said hidden.
Figaro in the bottom, imitating Bartolo's movements, and sayings.
The Count, Rosina and Figaro.
Bartolo coming back, and sayings.
Bartolo, the Count and Rosina.
The Count, and Rosina.
Bartolo, Figaro and sayings.
Don Basilio and sayings.
Bartolo, the Count, Rosina and Figaro.
The scene is obscured and a symphony is heard that describes a storm. Bartolo, and Don Basilio with a lantern of paper in his hand.
Rosina alone, bedroom with light.
Bartolo returns with a light, and said.
Rosina alone, pulls out the handkerchief, and leaves her crying.
The Count and Figaro, dressed, appear at the window.
Rosina, and sayings.
Don Basilio with the Notaro, and sayings.
Bartolo with an Alcade, of the Alguazili, and Servi with torches, and sayings. Bartolo enters, sees the Count, kissing the hand of Rosina, and Figaro hugging grotesquely Don Basilio.
Versione di Napoli, Teatro dei Fiorentini, 1787.
